description:
We are 9 Grah Scouts—a team of space lovers and tech builders inspired by India’s nine planets (Navagraha), the mystery of Planet X, and NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope. We love taking NASA’s free space data and turning it into cool, useful projects.

If you are excited about space and want to build something awesome together, join our team! We are looking for teammates who can help with coding, data analysis, app design, or making our final presentation video.
summary:
For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we built 9Graha Scout, an easy-to-use website that helps people explore Planet X and Sphere X.

What we built: A simple web app that shows space data and planet orbits in a clean, visual way.

How it helps: Space data is usually very confusing and full of complicated numbers. Our app turns that heavy science into simple pictures and easy facts anyone can understand.

Why it matters: You shouldn't need to be a rocket scientist to enjoy space. Our tool lets students and everyday people explore distant worlds and learn about the universe in seconds.
details: What Does It Do & How Does It Work? 9Graha Scout is an interactive web platform that allows users to explore data and visualizations related to Planet X (hypothetical outer solar system bodies/Planet Nine) and Sphere X (spatial/celestial mapping and NASA's SPHEREx mission concepts). Users visit the web app to view simplified orbital paths, spatial models, and key astronomical facts. Instead of reading raw spreadsheets or scientific papers, users interact with a clean, visual interface embedded directly on the site to click through objects, compare planetary data, and learn how scientists track distant phenomena. Benefits & Intended Impact Simplifies Complex Science: Translates heavy astronomical and telescopic data into bite-sized, visual insights that students, teachers, and everyday space fans can grasp quickly. Sparks Curiosity & Citizen Science: Lowers the barrier to entry for space exploration, inspiring young learners and non-scientists to engage with NASA’s ongoing search for undiscovered worlds and cosmic origins. Accessible Anywhere: Because it runs directly in a web browser, anyone with a phone or computer can explore it without downloading heavy software. Tools, Software & Tech Stack Web Hosting & Embedding: Google Sites (for clean, full-page public deployment). Frontend & Visualization: [e.g., HTML, CSS, JavaScript / React / Three.js / Canva / Figma] for building the interactive interface and space visuals. Data & Research: NASA open-source datasets, SPHEREx mission archives, and Kuiper Belt orbital data. What Makes It Creative? The name 9Graha Scout blends cultural heritage—Navagraha (the traditional nine celestial bodies in Indian astronomy)—with modern deep-space exploration (the search for the elusive 9th planet, Planet X, and wide-sky mapping like Sphere X). Combining ancient celestial curiosity with modern, interactive web design makes the project memorable and relatable. Key Factors Our Team Considered User-Friendliness: We prioritized a clutter-free layout so users wouldn't feel overwhelmed by astrophysics jargon. Accuracy vs. Simplicity: We worked carefully to ensure the planetary facts and mission concepts remained scientifically accurate while still being simple enough for a middle-school student to understand. Accessibility & Speed: Embedding the experience as a lightweight, full-page web app ensured fast loading times across both desktop and mobile devices.
